workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
rationale: A registered Gray conversion wgray is captured into rgray_s1, but rgray_s2 drops bit 0 (line 9), so rgray_s1[0] starts no chain. This is a partly synchronised Gray pointer: CDC-017 is primary, and CDC-004 and CDC-032(a) also match per the spec. The site is the actual unsynchronised destination bit rgray_s1[0], not the readers' rgray_s2[0], a constant that no crossing rule names. Critical is false: the unsynchronised bit has no consumer, so no metastable value reaches logic. The harm is functional truncation of the pointer (data_o carries only Gray bit 1). There is no FIFO, so FIFO functional claims are excluded. Raw rst_n release, recovery/removal and physical timing remain external obligations outside this label.

labels.rationale: rgray_s2 forces bit zero to zero instead of carrying rgray_s1[0]. The Gray word therefore has an incomplete synchronization path and loses a changing source bit. This is a malformed pointer-like transfer even though bit zero does not feed an unsafe first-stage consumer.
